input: Sort out international health insurance for expats

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether this is for one individual, a couple, a family, or a group of employees changes the type of plan, pricing tiers, and underwriting requirements entirely.
Whether the task means just researching options, getting quotes, or fully purchasing and activating a policy determines how much work is left and what the immediate next steps are.
The destination country (or countries) directly controls which insurers are eligible, what local regulations apply, and whether a global vs. regional plan is needed.
A monthly or annual budget ceiling will immediately filter out providers and plan tiers, making it the single biggest shortlisting factor.
Coverage priorities — e.g. routine GP visits, dental, mental health, maternity, emergency evacuation — vary enormously and change which plan is the best fit.
Knowing when coverage needs to start reveals whether there is time to do thorough research or whether speed is critical, affecting the entire approach.
Understanding whether 'done well' means cheapest viable plan, most comprehensive cover, or a trusted brand with strong claims support will resolve trade-off decisions throughout the process.

gold.taskTitle: Sort out international health insurance for expats
gold.taskDescription: Research, compare, and secure an appropriate international health insurance plan for one or more people living abroad.

questions.title: Who exactly needs to be covered by this policy?
questions.description: Establish whether the insurance is for a single adult, a couple, a family with children, or a group of employees, as this determines the plan category and pricing structure.

questions.title: Which country or countries will the person be living in?
questions.description: Identify the destination(s) to determine eligible insurers, regional vs. worldwide plans, and any local legal requirements for health coverage.

questions.title: What is the maximum monthly or annual premium budget?
questions.description: Pin down a hard or soft budget ceiling so plans can be shortlisted by affordability from the outset.

questions.title: Which coverage areas matter most to you?
questions.description: Identify priority benefits such as routine outpatient care, dental, mental health, maternity, or emergency evacuation, to match the plan to real needs.

questions.title: Does this need to be active, or just researched and compared?
questions.description: Clarify whether the goal is to produce a shortlist and recommendation, get live quotes, or actually purchase and activate a policy, so the scope of work is clear.

questions.title: When does coverage need to start?
questions.description: Determine the required start date to understand urgency, application lead times, and whether any gap in coverage needs to be bridged.

questions.title: What does the ideal outcome look like to you?
questions.description: Understand whether success means the lowest viable cost, the broadest possible cover, a well-known insurer with strong claims support, or something else — resolving the key trade-offs throughout.
